data.content_ref: inline:The 'Redundancy Paradox' mechanism asserts that a coordination layer becomes a single point of failure as redundancy increases, but this conflates redundancy with distribution. A large service with strictly more total internal redundancy can use partitioned/sharded coordination (multiple independent consensus groups) or formally verified consensus logic. The mechanism provides no causal link showing why added redundancy must necessarily increase coordination complexity rather than, e.g., reducing it via isolated failure domains.
